title: Padding Probe on a Stand-In Judge
description: A pure-Python probe that appends a padding string to three essays and watches whether a crude judge rewards the extra words.
source: draft: opencode free model + edit: codex

steps.description: `SAMPLES` holds three short essays. `s01` is a long argument that cites two sources and answers an objection. `s02` is a short hedged version, and `s03` stays general and off the question.
`PAD` is two sentences of praise that add words without adding substance. The probe appends it to each essay to see whether the judge rewards length.
`stand_in_judge` takes a text and splits off its first sentence. The docstring says the length bonus on directness is planted on purpose, so this judge carries a known flaw to find.

`levels` scores three criteria with simple string checks. `claims_cited` counts open parentheses and caps at 4. `directness` looks for `should` in the first sentence and falls back to anywhere in the text. `counterargument` looks for `Some argue` together with `but`.

steps.question: The judge adds a length bonus when the text runs over 50 words. `s01` is already 89 words and already at directness 4. What does the bonus do for `s01`?
steps.answer: Nothing. The bonus raises directness by one level but caps at 4, and `s01` is already there, so its directness stays put and its delta is zero.

steps.description: The header prints the column names, then the loop judges each essay twice: once as written and once with `PAD` appended. The inner loop prints one row per criterion with the before level, the after level, and the signed delta.
Run it. The header prints, and the loop starts with the first sample.
Inside `stand_in_judge`, the first sentence is split off so the directness check can look at it on its own.
The rows print. `directness` rises by 1 for `s02` and `s03` but stays flat for `s01`. The length bonus had nowhere to go on a sample already over 50 words and already at level 4.
